threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it 'the Tube' instead of just 'the Overground' when you're in Hackney. But hey, we appreciate your enthusiasm!
Caught a whiff of fried plantain on the 35 last night, and a group of teens had a full-on dance-off. Best night bus ride I’ve had in ages!

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I knew I was really home when I found a café that serves a proper Turkish breakfast, and the owner remembers my name after just one visit.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: In Friedrichshain, it's normal to see people using old subway maps as art. They turn worn-out BVG schedules into unique wall hangings. It's all about repurposing here.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know a local when they can name every taco truck on Mission and still complain about the price of a burrito from La Taqueria.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Last week, the bus driver asked a rider to pick up the empty bottles rolling around. Everyone cheered, but no one helped. Classic SF moment.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists assume every square is a party spot. But locals know to avoid plaça del Sol on weekends—it's just a loud drink fest.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: They always stare at the metro map like it’s written in hieroglyphics, while locals just breeze through with their eyes on their phones.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still stop at the pedestrian crossings, waiting for the green man, even on a quiet street. The locals know it’s really just a suggestion.
Last night on the 196, a guy serenaded the bus with a ukulele. Somehow made the 2am ride feel like a late-night festival.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I was grabbing a late-night Döner, and saw a group of kids setting up a mini-concert by the park. Just another night in Neukölln, where the unexpected is the norm.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: You ever notice how nearly every U-Bahn station has a different art exhibit? It's like a free gallery tour underground, with surprise pieces around every corner.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a true local by their instinctive dodge of the BART Civic Center station after a loud bang. Tourists don’t even check the alerts.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a glimpse of the Muni driver stopping mid-route to help a lost tourist with directions—only in SF will you see kindness like that on a hectic bus.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists always think Gràcia is just about the Gaudí vibe, but it's the little corner bakeries at dawn that keep this place real.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their endless confusion at the Gaixample street signs; they can’t quite figure out which way to go.
